chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man and Muhammad ibn Sinan and Fadala, from Al-Husayn, all from Ibn Muskān, from Sulayman ibn Khālid, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him)
Regarding the making up of the Witr prayer, he said: 'Make it up as Witr always.'

key_terms.اقْضِهِ: Make it up / Perform its qada

ai.seo_question: How should the Witr prayer be made up if it is missed?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the definitive ruling for making up the Witr prayer, emphasizing that it must always be performed as an odd number of units (witr) to preserve its distinct identity as a concluding prayer. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that Witr is not merely a single rak'ah but a flexible prayer structure that retains its 'odd' characteristic even when compensated for later, distinguishing it from the obligatory Fajr prayer.
